skill1: Sea Breeze: DEF ▼ 1.9% of the skill user's DEF, stacks up to 50 time(s) and lasts for 3 sec. (magnitude only — the named status window IS modeled)
Activates when HP falls below 70%. Affects self and 2 other ally unit(s) with the highest final ATK (except the skill user).

caveats: ⛑ Storm magnitude is an UNMEASURED estimate. The kit deals 4.52% of final ATK per Sea Breeze stack, once per second for 7 sec; the shipped atkPct 22.6 assumes a ~5-stack steady state (see flags). The stack pool is dynamic and 3-sec-decaying, so it cannot be encoded as a `resource`/`perResource` pool (resources do not decay and would ratchet toward the 50 cap).

⛑ Sea Breeze's DEF ▼ is a FLAT reduction scaled by the CASTER's DEF applied to the boss. The schema has no enemy-DEF-reduction channel (`defPct` is self-scoped and documented inert; `enemy` targets resolve to an empty set for buff effects), so the debuff's damage contribution — which is a TEAM-WIDE lift, not a self buff — is currently uncredited. This UNDER-models mast.

⛑ The skill1 HP<70% branch (Critical Damage ▲ 50.94% to self + 2 highest-final-ATK allies, continuous) is NOT modeled: the sim has no HP pool and no HP-threshold trigger primitive. If a real fight shows it firing, the whole crit-damage buff is missing from every mast comp — this is the single largest known gap in this baseline.

⛑ skill1's trigger is 2 CRITICAL hits with normal attacks; the schema's `hitCount` cannot filter for crits, so count is a crit-rate-derived round count (see flags). It affects only whether the Sea Breeze window is open, not any magnitude.

⛑ skill2 is encoded as a `passive` trigger carrying durationSec 30 to express "at the start of battle … for 30 sec". If the engine re-applies passive blocks continuously rather than once at setup, this would become a whole-fight crit-rate buff and OVER-credit the team — verify against a buffApply/expiresFrame read before trusting it.
Storm ticks are left DoT-default non-crit and Full-Burst-by-timing (no `noFb`), per the standing conventions — both are unmeasured for this unit.
The burst Max HP grant is recorded for kit completeness; ally-granted Max HP does not feed a teammate's HP→ATK conversion, so only the self block can ever be offensively live.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⛑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. mast is an SMG/Electric/Supporter/Burst II crit enabler with an enemy-DEF-shred status. skill1 stamps the named status Sea Breeze on the boss off normal-attack crits (status window modeled; the caster-DEF-scaled flat DEF ▼ has no schema channel and is unmodeled), plus an HP-threshold crit-damage branch that the sim cannot express. skill2 is a battle-start 30-sec Critical Rate ▲ 23.56% to self + the 2 highest-final-ATK other allies (split into a self block and an alliesTopAtk/excludeSelf/byFinalAtk block — the schema has no single "self and N others" target). The burst repeats that target split for a 7-sec Max HP + Critical Damage grant and adds Storm, a 1-sec-interval 7-tick DoT gated on the Sea Breeze status whose per-tick magnitude scales with the live stack count — shipped as a static stack-count estimate.

flags.reasoning: Storm's magnitude mirrors the live Sea Breeze stack count, which is a steady state, not the 50 cap: stacks are gained per 2 normal-attack crits and each expires after 3 sec. At an SMG cadence of ~20 rounds/s with ~76% fire uptime (120 ammo, 111f reload) and a ~15% base crit rate, that is ~1.5 stacks/s → ~4–5 concurrent. Inside her own skill2 window (first 30 sec, crit ~38.6%) it roughly doubles to ~10–12, so early bursts mirror far more stacks than late ones; ~5 is the rotation-weighted middle over a 180-sec fight. Both the cadence and the crit rate feeding this are themselves unmeasured.
flags.recipe: Record a fight with mast bursting; in the 7 sec after her burst banner, read the 7 Storm popups and divide each by a same-frame normal-hit popup scaled to 4.52%/8.73% of the normal multiplier — the quotient IS the mirrored stack count per tick. Confirm the early-vs-late asymmetry by comparing her first burst (inside the skill2 crit window) against a burst after t=60s; if the two differ materially, the static atkPct must be replaced by a per-tick dynamic read rather than retuned.

flags.reasoning: The kit trigger is 2 CRITICAL hits with normal attacks; the schema's hitCount counts all rounds and cannot filter crits, so count = 2 / crit rate. At ~15% base crit that is ~13 rounds; inside her own skill2 crit window it would be ~5. At SMG cadence 13 rounds is ~0.65 sec, so the Sea Breeze window is effectively continuous while she fires and this value is near-inert for the burst gate — it would only matter if a future model made the stack count itself dynamic.
flags.recipe: Not worth a dedicated measurement while Sea Breeze is used only as a binary gate. It becomes load-bearing the moment the DEF ▼ or a dynamic Storm stack count is modeled — at that point derive it from the sheet crit rate at scope lock rather than measuring, and verify by checking that the status never lapses during a firing window in footage.

flags.field: skill1 — HP<70% branch (absent from the override)
flags.estimate: If measured to fire, encode as two blocks (target self / alliesTopAtk{2,excludeSelf,byFinalAtk}) with buff critDamagePct 50.94 and NO durationSec ('continuously'), on trigger {kind:'interval', sec:≈45} so the buff switches on at the measured drop time and then persists.
flags.reasoning: The sim models no incoming damage, so no unit's HP ever falls, and there is no HP-threshold trigger primitive. The two available encodings are both wrong in a known direction: `passive` credits +50.94% crit damage to three units for the full 180 sec (a large unearned buff), and omission credits none of it. Faithful > fit, so this baseline omits it and flags it rather than shipping the optimistic reading. The interval-trigger form above is the only way to express a mid-fight switch-on, and its `sec` would be a measured value, not a guess.
flags.recipe: From raid footage, timestamp the frame mast's HP bar first crosses 70% (and whether it does so at all under scope-lock conditions). If it never crosses, the omission is CORRECT and should be recorded as such. If it crosses at time T, land the interval encoding with sec=T and re-run the board A/B — note this changes three units' crit damage, so it is a rotation-wide movement, not a mast-only one.

flags.field: skill1 — Sea Breeze DEF ▼ (absent from the override)
flags.estimate: Unmodelable in the current schema. Real magnitude at cap = 50 × 1.9% = 95% of mast's own DEF subtracted flat from boss DEF.
flags.reasoning: The reduction is scaled by the CASTER's DEF and applied to the enemy, and the boss-DEF term sits in the damage formula for every unit — so this is a team-wide damage lift, the opposite of a skippable defensive line. No StatKey expresses it: defPct is self-scoped and documented inert, and buff effects targeting `enemy` resolve to an empty target set (only the boss-held damageTakenPct path special-cases the boss). Re-expressing it as damageTakenPct would be a fudge, since converting a flat DEF subtraction into a damage-taken percentage requires the boss's DEF value and the formula's DEF term, neither of which is being measured here.
flags.recipe: Two-part. (1) Derive the ceiling: with mast's DEF from the scope-lock class table and the boss DEF constant, compute what a 95%-of-caster-DEF subtraction does to the formula's DEF term — if the shift is below the noise floor the gap is academic and should be recorded as such. (2) If material, measure directly: same comp, same teammate, compare that teammate's normal-hit popup values before mast's first crit (no stacks) against values during sustained fire (stacks up), holding buff state constant — the popup ratio backs out the effective DEF reduction. That measurement, not this baseline, is what would justify adding an enemy-DEF channel to the schema.

flags.field: base weapon cadence tuple (SMG, 120 ammo, 111f reload)
flags.reasoning: Mandatory ⛑: datamined rate_of_fire and reloadFrames are known-unreliable fields, and a nominal rate is not the effective rate because the game fires on 60fps frame boundaries. Everything in this baseline that depends on shots-per-second — the hitCount trigger translation and, through the stack steady state, the entire Storm magnitude — inherits this uncertainty.
flags.recipe: Read the ammo counter across a full magazine in footage (rounds spent per second measures the disputed quantity directly, unlike full-burst counts which are downstream of gauge). Confirm against the existing SMG cadence pins in the repo before deriving anything new.

flags.field: burst[2].effects[0] — Storm crit + Full Burst treatment
flags.estimate: non-crit (schema default); Full Burst applied by tick timing (no noFb)
flags.reasoning: Per convention DoT ticks are validated non-crit on most carriers and crit is opt-in only where measured, and function-damage riders take Full Burst by landing timing with noFb default OFF and measured-only. Storm is cast at burst time but runs 7 sec, so its later ticks land inside the Full Burst window and currently receive the +50% major — that is the default, not a finding.
flags.recipe: In the same footage used for the magnitude read, check Storm popup colour (orange + icon = crit) across the 7 ticks, and compare the in-FB ticks against the out-of-FB ticks for a ~1.5× step. Only set crit:true or noFb:true if the footage shows it.
